children: Evercore ISI says investors should look beyond the obvious AI winners after Democrats took control of Congress, naming
Amphenol, Arista Networks, Apple
, Cisco
and Motorola Solutions
as technology stocks that could hold up better in a tougher regulatory environment.
The firm's argument starts with data centers.

Evercore believes stricter regulation around new projects could weigh on sentiment toward AI infrastructure companies, particularly in states such as Texas, Georgia and Ohio where data-center construction has become a bigger political issue.
But the consequences would not be uniformly negative.

Slower construction could temper demand for memory products such as DRAM and NAND, potentially easing a major cost headwind for companies including Apple and PC makers. Apple previously said higher memory costs represented roughly a
140-basis-point gross-margin headwind
in the December quarter.
Evercore called Apple a particularly defensive name because its earnings depend more on
iPhone mix, pricing and Services
than on new data-center construction. The firm also pointed to resilient demand and the potential for gross-margin recovery.
Amphenol offers a different type of protection.

Evercore sees the connector maker as a diversified way to retain AI exposure because its business spans high-speed data, power and optical products alongside defense, aerospace and industrial markets. That reduces dependence on any single AI architecture or customer.

Arista remains Evercore's preferred high-quality networking exposure, while Cisco could benefit from campus refresh cycles, optics and Silicon One. Motorola Solutions stands apart because its public-safety communications business is less tied to AI spending and more resistant to macro weakness.
Investor Takeaway
I think the most interesting part of Evercore's call is that
a slowdown in AI infrastructure spending does not automatically mean investors should abandon technology altogether
Instead, it may shift the leadership.

Companies whose earnings depend directly on ever-rising data-center construction could face more political and permitting risk, while diversified hardware, networking and consumer-tech names may look relatively safer.
Apple is probably the clearest example because tighter data-center development could indirectly reduce memory inflation while leaving its core iPhone and Services engine largely untouched.
For investors, the key things to watch are
data-center regulation, memory pricing, Apple gross margins, networking demand and whether capital rotates from pure AI infrastructure plays into more defensive technology names
The election may not end the AI trade.
It could change which tech stocks investors want to own.

title: Evercore Names 5 Tech Stocks to Own After Blue Wave
